item.title: Together Again, 1960–2026: Perspectives from UC Davis' Fine Arts Collection — Wed Oct 7, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description:
This ongoing collection exhibition traces a history of art forged from this place. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, “Together Again” proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Davis Farmers Market — Wed Oct 7, 3:00 PM — Central Park
item.description:
Year-round at Central Park in downtown Davis, thousands gather each week to shop for what is grown, raised, and made locally at our markets. We are dedicated to bringing farmers right to your table, so we stay open rain or shine. Walk rows of stalls lined with an array of fruits and vegetables, including certified organic produce, choice meats, chicken, seafood, wine, local eggs and honey. Choose from a variety of fresh-baked goods, plants, flowers and gifts. Enjoy a picnic from one of our many food stands, made from market ingredients. See the vendor list here: https://www.davisfarmersmarket.org/our-sellers/ Farmers Market Hours Central Park: Saturdays 8a–1p (year-round), and Wednesdays 3p–6p (September through March); 4p–8p (April through August) UC Davis – North Quad: Wednesdays 10a–1:30p (fall and spring quarters) Sutter Davis Hospital: Thursdays 10a–1p (May through September) Sutter Medical Center, Sacramento: Thursdays 2:30p–5:30p
Source: The Dirt

item.title: DJUSD Board Meetings — Thu Dec 3, 6:30 PM — City Hall Community Chambers
item.description:
DJUSD Board meetings offer insight on how the school district remains responsive to the community’s values, beliefs, and priorities. The Board meetings occur on every first and third Thursday, in the City of Davis Community Chambers. 23 Russell Boulevard. Public session starts at 6:30 PM. Meetings are cablecast live on Channel 17 (Comcast) or streamed on the DJUSD-TV website.
The Davis Joint Unified School District’s Board of Education is comprised of five community members, responsible for setting district policy, approving the budget, and hiring the superintendent for schools in Davis, California. The agendas for the meetings are posted at least 72 hours in advance.
For more information on special meetings, agendas, public comment, and more, visit the DJUSD Board site.
Source: Hate-Free Together

item.title: Sophie Weston Chien in conversation with Natalia Duong & Akshita Sivakumar — Mon Oct 5, 4:45 PM — Cruess Hall
item.description:
This conversation will build off Weston Chien’s recent series Touching Toxicity, a body of textile work that maps contamination and remediation across the East Bay. Industrial heavy metals and volatile organic compounds have contaminated the soil and groundwater of the Bay Area, an issue made even more fraught when rising sea levels can push these materials further to the surface. Environmental remediation often focuses on removing the harm wrought by toxicity; sites are returned to a pre-toxic state through the removal or capping of harmful materials. Touching Toxicity considers what a framework of return means given larger and longer trends of environmental harm. Together, the panelists will discuss toxicity, remediation, and how artistic and design practice might offer new timescales and tactics for environmental justice.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Davis Parent University Presents Ana Homayoun — Tue Oct 6, 7:00 PM — Richard Brunelle Performance Hall
item.description:
BRUNELLE THEATER, Davis: Please join Davis Parent University (DPU) for a FIRESIDE CHAT between Ana Homayoun, executive functioning strategist & academic advisor, and Pamela Wu, Director of News and Media Relations for UC Davis Health, as they unpack how to help our kids adapt, adjust, and course-correct. Ana Homayoun is the acclaimed author of “Getting In Is Not Enough: The New Blueprint for Success beyond Grades, Test Scores, and College Admission.” Ana and Pam will share the stage for a 50 minute moderated conversation, followed by a 30 minute audience Q&A and then a book signing. FREE tickets are available at davisparentuniversity.com.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Reflecting Images: Christianity and AI in Conversation — Tue Oct 6, 7:00 PM — The Episcopal Church of St. Martin
item.description: The conversation about artificial intelligence, or AI, has become a significant part of our everyday lives, to the point that so much of the current economy is bound up in this technology. It’s hard to listen to a newscast or read a headline without some mention of AI, either as ground-breaking technology that will make our lives easier and more efficient, or as a possible threat to human existence. Three local pastors have come together out of the belief that “people of faith ought to be able to think and speak intelligently about AI and navigate the many issues it involves while holding onto the values that guide them in their faith,” according to Mae Forrest Barnes, Ph.D., an Episocpalian with a background in theology and ethics and a special focus in accessibility, science, and theological ethics. Join **Rev. Rola Al-Ashkar** for a five-week journey exploring how our life experiences shape the way we respond to stress, conflict, belonging, and relationships. Through storytelling, guided reflection, and gentle body-centered (somatic) practices, participants will develop tools for greater self-awareness, emotional resilience, and compassionate listening. item.title: Author talk by Peter Flax: Why We Ride — Thu Oct 22, 5:30 PM — Shields Library
item.description:
Join us for an inspiring and enlightening look at the reasons that make people fall in love with bicycle riding! Author Peter Flax will share his insights into the creation and production of Live to Ride: Finding Joy and Meaning on a Bicycle, his 2024 book which explores the unifying dynamics of bicycle culture.
The book argues that everyone who rides—whether they commute, enjoy nature, or race—has more in common than they might realize. Part of the discussion will focus on a section contextualizing the significance of groundbreaking bike lanes constructed decades ago in Davis—and how Flax was aided by photography and documents from our Archives and Special Collections Department.
This talk is free and open to all. Please register in advance to reserve your spot.
